data.narrative:
Charge Robotics is a Series B-stage company in Housing & Construction founded by Banks Hunter and Max Justicz. The company has raised $43.9M to date. The valuation universe consists of four private peers operating in adjacent construction technology and materials segments: Plantd Materials, Cuby Technologies, Cover, and Somos. No direct public comparables exist in this emerging subsector.

Given the limited methodological applicability at this stage, a single stage-progression approach was employed. Using total capital raised ($44M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-round step-ups, the analysis derives an implied valuation of $83M. This represents the central case in a triangulated range.

The valuation analysis supports a range of $71M to $96M, with $83M as the median point. This range reflects uncertainty inherent in applying stage-progression mechanics to a single company in a nascent sector with sparse comparable transaction data. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 1.9x step-up multiplier to Charge Robotics' specific risk profile and growth trajectory, the composition and relevance of the four-company peer set, and the absence of public market benchmarks for validation. Investors should weight this analysis alongside detailed operating metrics and capital efficiency trends before commitment.
